summary: William George Grey was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who received an honorary M.A. from the University of Cambridge around 1931. He served as Lecturer in Urdu at Gonville and Caius College from 1929 to 1940.

Sinologist William H. Nienhauser, Jr. studied at Indiana University Bloomington under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, as well as at Bonn. At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he became full professor in 1983 and Halls-Bascom Professor in 1995.

William H. Wiser worked in Indology, studying at the University of Chicago and Cornell University (Ph.D. circa 1931-1933). He held a post at Sam Higginbottom University in 1915 and served as Professor of Rural Sociology at North India Theological College.

Indology scholar William Harlen Gilbert, Jr. earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago around 1930-1935. He taught sociology at Auburn University from 1936 to 1937 and held a post at the Library of Congress from circa 1941 to 1972.

Historian and Indologist William Harrison Moreland was educated at Clifton College and Trinity College, Cambridge (LL.B. circa 1886-1889). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1889 to 1914.
William Hay Macnaghten, a scholar in Indology, completed his education at Charterhouse School around 1806-1809 and studied at Fort William College in 1816.

William Henry Carmichael Smyth was a linguistics and Indology scholar who attended Charterhouse School. He later served as Resident Superintendent at the Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1822 to 1824.

Linguist and Indologist William Henry Coxe studied Classics and Sanskrit at Balliol College, Oxford. He worked at the British Museum from 1861 to 1865, joining the Indian Education Service and holding King's College London's unpaid chair of Sanskrit in 1865.
William Henry Fox Talbot worked in history and archaeology. He received his education at Harrow School until 1815 and subsequently studied at Trinity College, Cambridge between 1817 and 1821.

William Henry Hale was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his B.A. and Ph.D. at Yale University between circa 1856 and 1863, and earned an LL.B. from Albany Law School around 1860-1861.

Scholar of philosophy and religion William Henry Harris earned degrees from Southern Nazarene and Boston Universities, and studied under T. M. P. Mahadevan at Madras. He worked at the University of Arkansas and Southern Illinois University Edwardsville.

Indologist and religious studies scholar William Henry Mill earned degrees at Trinity College and Cambridge. He served as Principal of Bishop's College in Kolkata (1820-1838) and as Christian Advocate and Regius Professor of Hebrew at Cambridge.

Historian and Indologist William Henry Sleeman served in the Bengal Army (1809-1854), rising to Major-General. He was General Superintendent of the Thuggee and Dacoity Department from 1835 and Resident at the University of Lucknow from 1849 to 1856.
Indologist and historian William Henry Sykes founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. He also served as President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1858.

Linguist and Indologist William Henry Wait studied at Northwestern, Allegheny College, Berlin, and Bonn. He taught at Illinois Wesleyan University and later at the University of Michigan, where he was Professor of Modern Languages from circa 1904 to 1925.

Indologist and historian William Hoey earned an M.A. from Queen's University Belfast. He served as Reader in Hindustani and Indian History at the University of Oxford from around 1906 to 1919 and at Trinity College Dublin in 1910.

Linguist and Indologist William Holme Williams earned his A.B. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1876. He taught there continuously, becoming Professor of Hebrew and Sanskrit in 1889 and Professor of Semitic Languages and Hellenistic Greek (1892-1917).
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge around 1921-1925. He subsequently taught John Hurrell Crook and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1932 to 1969.

William Hook Morley was an Indologist and historian called to the bar at the Middle Temple in 1840. He served as a member and later Librarian (1859) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

William Howard Campbell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh, earning an M.A. and B.D. around 1876-1882. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1884 to 1903.
